audit.whatIsWrong: The page rates the lane 8.5/10 hard with Swain winning five of seven stages, while its own prose says the opposite and Illaoi wins 55.99%.
audit.why: whys[1] 'your W-dash reset lets you slam tentacles and win trades', whys[2] 'your tentacle field grinds him', whys[3] 'keep your all-in above what Swain can trade back', whys[4] 'Level-6 R out-damages Swain's Demonic Ascension drain', whys[5] 'First item plus tentacle uptime wins any extended fight', mid 'Levels 2 through first-item are firmly yours', early 'Swain only leads at level 1'. packet.levelChart agrees exactly: Swain, then Illaoi for five stages, then Swain. The full layer even sets diff to FAV while tone is the red #ff5d6c and report[14] says 'Hard matchup' — three different verdicts on one page.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 flipped to Illaoi in both layers as one atomic group, ratings raised, diffRating cut from 8.5/10 to 5/10, tone set to the favoured green, and the difficulty and final-rating prose brought with them. Row 0 and row 6 already read Swain and stay.

audit.why: The four spikes are placed right — level 1 poke, the 3-5 tentacle window, the level-6 Leap of Faith wall against a 120-second Demonic Ascension, and Swain's item-scaling drain-tank late. Only the chart rows around them were wrong.
audit.corrected: Kept; the 12-second Nevermove number was added to the 3-5 spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nevermove is described only as a root with a vague 'long cooldown', and Death's Hand only as generic poke.
audit.why: Riot on Nevermove (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, 850 range): 'Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits.' The outgoing wave does not root — the return does, and that return trip is the thing you sidestep. For an immobile champion whose whole pattern needs to reach him, that is the single most useful mechanic on the page and it was missing. Riot on Death's Hand (Q, 7/6/5/4/3s, 750 range): the bolts 'pierce through enemies' and 'Enemies hit take more damage for each bolt they are struck by' — standing at the edge of the cone eats one bolt instead of the fan, which is concrete positioning the page never gave.
audit.corrected: The return-trip root with its 12s cooldown written into dosFull[2], report[5], the cooldown block and spikes[0]; the per-bolt stacking written into whys[0], report[5] and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns tracks Demonic Ascension as the matchup-defining cooldown with no number, and Nevermove is absent.
audit.why: Demonic Ascension is 120s and, per Riot, 'indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions' — it is not a window you wait out mid-fight. The lane cooldown that actually decides whether you can run the pattern is Nevermove at 12s rank 1; Death's Hand is 7s and Vision of Empire 22s.
audit.corrected: Nevermove promoted to the tracked cooldown with its real number; Demonic Ascension kept with its 120s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern' names no heal source.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock: 'Swain's ravens collect Soul Fragments that heal him and permanently increase his maximum health', and Vision of Empire grants him a Soul Fragment on every champion it hits. So his sustain is a resource he farms off you, and it also grows his HP pool permanently — which is why the _missing file flags both needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated for this pairing.
audit.corrected: report[8] now names Soul Fragments as the healing.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Demonic Ascension and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5/10. The lane is decided by how well you dodge Nevermove's return and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10, Swain carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Favoured matchup — difficulty 5/10, Swain carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Swain's level-1 Q Death's Hand poke beats your not-yet-ramped tentacle field.
edits.after: Death's Hand stacks per bolt, so his level-1 poke beats your empty field.

edits.before: Poke you at level 1 with Q Death's Hand before your tentacles ramp
edits.after: Catch you full-width with Q so every Death's Hand bolt lands

edits.before: After the level-1 poke phase, you take over. W Harsh Lesson dashes you onto Swain to reset and slam tentacles, and if he lands his E Nevermove root you can often still out-slam him — punish every whiffed E by W-ing in during the long cooldown while your tentacle field grinds his health.
edits.after: After the level-1 poke phase, you take over. W Harsh Lesson dashes you onto Swain to reset and slam tentacles, and Nevermove only roots on its return trip — sidestep the wave coming back, then W in during the 12 seconds it is down while your tentacle field grinds his health.

edits.before: Swain wastes Demonic Ascension — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on the way back — sidestep the return, not the throw.

edits.before: Track Swain's Demonic Ascension: His drain. Don’t fight into it. When it is down — Slam him in your field.
edits.after: Nevermove roots on its return trip, 12s at rank 1; Death's Hand stacks per bolt, so stand at the edge.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain. Don’t fight into it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Nevermove (12s at rank 1): it roots on the return, and every whiff is 12s of free field. - Demonic Ascension 120s: never fight into the drain. - Test of Spirit 16s: never on chip. - Leap of Faith: kill windows.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield + pot vs the poke. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Mercury's Treads. Executioner's Calling early — his healing fights your pattern.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield + pot vs the poke. Core: Iceborn Gauntlet  (the slow makes tentacles land), then Sterak's Gage; boots Mercury's Treads. Executioner's Calling — every Soul Fragment heals him.

notes: This page had three different verdicts printed on it at once: diff FAV, tone red, report[14] 'Hard matchup', diffRating 8.5/10 — against a 55.99% win rate and a chart that gave Swain five stages while every why[] gave them to Illaoi. The rating was cut to 5/10 rather than to the low numbers the mirror direction would imply, because Swain genuinely owns level 1 and the late game and the carry threat of 8/10 was left standing. focus.text still reads 'Swain Demonic Ascension'; the cooldown that decides the lane is Nevermove, so that field is worth a champion-level look. Standing Illaoi flag misfires left unwritten: Leap of Faith does not ground or grant untargetability, Test of Spirit does not slow.
